explanations: `GET /statements/latest` creates and persists a new statement on every call. GET must be safe, but here every page refresh, browser prefetch, proxy retry or monitoring probe inserts a statement and moves the next period's start, so customers get a stream of tiny statements covering arbitrary slivers of time. Statement generation should be a POST (or a scheduled job), with `latest` only reading the most recent stored statement.

`loadAccount` calls `findAccount(accountId, ownerId)`, which returns null for an account the caller doesn't own, and responds 404 account_not_found before the handler runs. No 403 path exists, the statement lookup never runs, and that lookup is also scoped by account id.

`openingBalanceMinor` etc. are `bigint`; JSON.stringify throws on bigint, and converting to number could lose precision above 2^53. Strings preserve exact minor units. Express sends numbers fine; string sorting of amounts is wrong anyway; currency is sent explicitly.

The handler loads the statement and calls `entriesBetween(account.id, statement.periodStart, statement.periodEnd)`. Nothing is snapshotted with the statement (only `entryCount` is stored), and there is no pagination or filtering by createdAt.
